name: Hurl
summary: Command line tool that runs HTTP requests from plain text files and checks responses.
features: chain HTTP requests in plain text
integrate tests in CI/CD with reports

steps.command: mkdir -p ~/.local/bin /tmp/hurl-install && INSTALL_DIR=/tmp/hurl-install VERSION=8.1.0 && curl --silent --location https://github.com/Orange-OpenSource/hurl/releases/download/$VERSION/hurl-$VERSION-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz | tar xvz -C $INSTALL_DIR && ls -l $INSTALL_DIR/hurl-$VERSION-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/bin/

pitfalls.readme_said: Precompiled binary (depending on libc >=2.35) available at GitHub release and works by extracting tar.gz and adding bin to PATH
pitfalls.actually_needed: Binary also requires libxml2.so.2 which is not present in this Debian trixie box; hurl fails to start with 'cannot open shared object file' and would need apt-get install libxml2

cat > /tmp/server.py <<'PY' from http.server import HTTPServer, BaseHTTPRequestHandler import json, urllib.parse class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler): def do_GET(self): path = self.path.split('?')[0] if path in ("/api/health", "/api/step1", "/api/step2", "/api/step3", "/"): self.send_response(200) self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json") self.end_headers() body = json.dumps({"status":"ok", "path": path}).encode() self.wfile.write(body) elif path == "/api/tests": self.send_response(200) self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json") self.send_header("X-Frame-Options", "SAMEORIGIN") self.end_headers() body = json.dumps({"status":"RUNNING","tests": list(range(25)), "id":"4568"}).encode() self.wfile.write(body) elif path == "/html": self.send_response(200) self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/html") self.end_headers() self.wfile.write(b"Hello world!

Hurl is a command line tool that runs HTTP requests
Hurl is a command line tool that runs HTTP requests defined in a simple plain text format.
Hurl, run and test HTTP requests with plain text.
it can be used for both fetching data and testing HTTP sessions.
It is well adapted for REST / JSON APIs
Hurl can also be used to test the performance of HTTP endpoints
but it's still the [curl] that we love
It can chain requests, capture values and evaluate queries on headers and body response.
Hurl can run HTTP requests but can also be used to test HTTP responses.
Finally, Hurl is easy to integrate in CI/CD, with text, JUnit, TAP and HTML reports
